Done. The export ran successfully on the first execution.

**What I did**
- Wrote `out/T3/solution.py`, a plain torch plus safetensors script. It reads the two input shards, casts tensors matching an anchored regex for the per-layer q, k, v, o, gate, up and down projections to bfloat16, and leaves everything else float32 and untouched.
- The script enforces the required checks before writing: 112 bfloat16 tensors, layer 0 q_proj is bfloat16, embeddings and lm_head are float32, 114 tensors total, unchanged key set. It exits non-zero on any failure.
- Sharding is greedy in sorted key order with a 256 MiB tensor-data budget. Oversized tensors go alone in their own shard. After writing, it re-opens every shard and verifies counts, budgets, and that the float32 tensors are bit-identical.

**Result in `out/T3/`**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Shards | 10 (2 solo float32 shards for embed_tokens and lm_head, 8 bf16 shards at exactly 256 MiB) |
| Tensors | 114 in index and on disk |
| bfloat16 tensors | 112 |
| Executions | 1, no failures |

The self-report is in `out/T3/REPORT.md`, listing torch 2.14.0 and safetensors 0.5.3 as the tools used and why I skipped the transformers export route.
